Together they form the combined hardware and software system of modern electronic music production.

音序器本身不產生聲音，而是透過調用各類音源模組來發聲，因此音色具有極強的可塑性與: A sequencer makes no sound itself; it sounds by calling up sound modules, so its timbre is extremely malleable and varied. Its timbres run from bright, sharp synth tones to warm, full imitations of strings, covering the range of almost every instrument. A software sequencer uses digital waveform synthesis and sampling to reproduce the character of traditional instruments accurately, and can also create virtual timbres that do not exist in nature. Its sound does not depend on a traditional resonating body but is presented through speakers or a monitoring system. Compared with the organic warmth of traditional instruments, a sequencer's timbre is more precise and more controllable, and can change style in an instant. This endlessly extendable quality is what makes it a core tool of modern music production, filling in the expressive limits of any single instrument.
音序器源於音樂盒、機械風琴、自動鋼琴等機械重現音樂的裝置。九世紀波斯班努穆薩兄弟: The sequencer descends from mechanical devices that reproduce music: the music box, the mechanical organ, the player piano. In ninth-century Persia the Banu Musa brothers used a hydraulic pipe organ and a steam-driven automatic flute with exchangeable pinned cylinders, early programmable music machines; in the twelfth century the Arab engineer al-Jazari used cam pins to control the rhythm of drummers. From the late eighteenth to the early nineteenth century, punched paper rolls and pinned-cylinder automatic instruments were widespread, and they continued into the mid-twentieth century. In the 1950s the RCA Mark II and Siemens synthesizers were still controlled by punched tape; after MIDI appeared in the 1980s, software sequencers, digital audio workstations and virtual instruments spread, and hardware sequencers moved inside keyboards and drum machines.
